items.title: CJC-1295 Explained: Does It Really Increase Growth Hormone?
items.summary: Does CJC-1295 really increase growth hormone? 🧬 CJC-1295 is often discussed alongside growth hormone, muscle growth, fat loss, recovery, and anti-aging—but CJC-1295 is not growth hormone. It's a synthetic analog of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to stimulate the pituitary gland, which can increase the body's own release of growth hormone (GH) and raise IGF-1 levels. Early human research involving the long-acting DAC form of CJC-1295 found that a single dose produced sustained increases in average growth hormone and IGF-1 levels. But there's an important distinction: Increasing GH and IGF-1 does NOT automatically prove that CJC-1295 builds muscle, burns fat, improves longevity, or reverses aging. Changing a biomarker and demonstrating a meaningful clinical benefit are two very different things. In this Peptide A to Z Short, we break down what CJC-1295 actually does, how the pituitary → GH → IGF-1 pathway works, and why it's important to separate human research from claims made online. 🧬 Follow Peptide A to Z for evidence-based coverage of peptides, clinical trials, longevity science, GLP-1 research, and emerging compounds. Peptide science without the hype. ⚠️ Educational and informational purposes only. Not medical advice. CJC-1295 is not FDA-approved for anti-aging, muscle building, or fat loss. #CJC1295 #Peptides #GrowthHormone #PeptideResearch #IGF1 ⚠️ DISCLAIMER This video is for educational purposes only. items.title: TB-500 is finally entering human research. 🧬
items.summary: TB-500 has been discussed for years in the peptide and biohacking communities for its potential role in recovery, tissue repair and healing. But there's an important catch: much of the excitement surrounding TB-500 has been based on preclinical research, animal studies, and research involving its parent molecule, thymosin beta-4—not robust human clinical evidence for TB-500 itself. Now that's beginning to change. A human clinical trial involving TB-500 is giving researchers an opportunity to start answering the questions that matter: What happens in humans? What does the safety data show? And do the proposed benefits actually translate beyond the laboratory? Popularity isn't the same thing as proof. We are building a vertically integrated pharmaceutical company with software for prescribing, telehealth, compounding, manufacturing, and delivery. We are starting with GLP-1s and peptides. The path to RonanRx is fairly unconventional. During the pandemic, I built one of the largest mask manufacturing factories in the US. We could make a million masks in a day. We converted raw polypropylene pellets into finished pallets of masks. I had a background in software from my YC W10 company, so we took a software approach to building our factory. We used machine learning and computer vision to optimize production. We also vertically integrated almost everything. It worked. We built an efficient manufacturing operation and grew the business to 50 million dollars in revenue. Then people actually stopped caring about masks. Fair enough. I stopped scrolling Instagram and quit biting my nails. But that was just the beginning. I was born with a congenital heart defect called aortic stenosis. items.title: GLP-1s Are Melting Fat — But What About Your MUSCLE?
items.summary: GLP-1 drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound can produce dramatic weight loss. But when someone loses 40 or 50 pounds, there's an important question most people aren't asking: How much of that weight was fat — and how much was lean mass? In this video, Peptide A to Z examines the growing concern around GLP-1 drugs and muscle loss. Research shows that people taking GLP-1 medications can lose measurable amounts of lean body mass along with fat. But the full story is more complicated than headlines suggesting these drugs simply “eat your muscle.” We break down: 💉 GLP-1 weight loss and lean mass 🔥 Fat loss vs. muscle loss 📊 What the STEP 1 semaglutide data actually showed 🫀 Why visceral fat matters 💪 Why preserving muscle becomes increasingly important with age 🧬 The new PROACT clinical trial 🔬 S-pindolol benzoate, also known as ACM-001.1 🏋️ Protein, resistance training and muscle preservation ⚖️ Why researchers are focusing on the quality of weight loss In the STEP 1 body-composition analysis, semaglutide was associated with approximately 19% lower total fat mass and 27% lower visceral fat, while lean body mass declined by about 10%. So yes, lean mass can decrease. But substantially more fat was lost, meaning overall body composition improved. Now researchers want to know whether they can do even better. The PROACT Phase 2 trial is studying whether an experimental drug called S-pindolol benzoate can help preserve lean body mass during semaglutide treatment. Researchers are also…

items.title: GLP-1 Pills Are Here — Are They Better Than the Shots?
items.summary: GLP-1 weight-loss pills are officially here. But are they actually better than injections — or do they come with the same risks in a different package? You may have seen Martha Stewart advertising Foundayo, Lilly's new once-daily GLP-1 pill. But Foundayo isn't simply an injectable GLP-1 turned into a tablet. Its active ingredient, orforglipron, is a non-peptide small molecule designed to activate the GLP-1 receptor. And it's not the only option. Wegovy is now available as an oral semaglutide tablet, giving patients another alternative to weekly GLP-1 injections. In this video, Peptide A to Z breaks down: 💊 GLP-1 pills vs. injections 🧬 How oral Wegovy and Foundayo are different ⚖️ The potential advantages and disadvantages of GLP-1 pills 📉 What clinical trials show about weight loss 🍽️ Appetite control and delayed gastric emptying ⚠️ Side effects and important safety considerations 💉 Daily pills vs. weekly injections 🔬 Why orforglipron isn't actually a peptide 📺 What to know about the Martha Stewart Foundayo campaign 🤔 And the big question: Are GLP-1 pills actually better than the shots? One of the most interesting developments is the science itself. Oral Wegovy contains the peptide semaglutide and uses a formulation designed to help it be absorbed orally. Foundayo takes a completely different approach: orforglipron is a small molecule rather than a peptide, but it targets the same GLP-1 receptor. That could have implications extending well beyond weight loss. But there's an…
